sheet_text: Design in-house policy on communication to consumers; use visualisations to ease non-technical stakeholder understanding
official_text: Design an in-house policy on communication to consumers that articulates the principles for transparency, e.g., define the purpose and context of communication to determine how and what to communicate. Use visualisations or other methods to ease non-technical stakeholders understanding of AI system functionality

sheet_text: Inform relevant stakeholders that AI is used in products and/or services
official_text: Inform relevant stakeholders that AI is used in your products and/or services

sheet_text: Implement mechanisms (labelling/disclaimers) to inform users when interacting with AI and accurately understand content lineage/origin
official_text: Implement mechanisms such as labelling or disclaimers to enable users, where possible and appropriate, to know when they are interacting with an AI system, and they accurately understand content lineage and origin

sheet_text: Communicate factors leading to AI decisions and that decision was partially/completely made by automated system
official_text: For decisions made or materially influenced by the AI system, communicate to those using or impacted by the system the: (a) factors leading to the decision, and (b) decision was partially or completely made by an automated system

sheet_text: Consult end users at earliest stages of development to communicate how technology is used
official_text: Consult end users at the earliest stages of AI system development to External communicate how the Documentary technology is used and end development how it will be deployed is

sheet_text: Publicly report relevant information (accuracy, intended use, limitations, risk assessment, mitigation measures); share AI Verify report
official_text: Publicly report relevant information (e.g., regarding accuracy, intended use cases, and limitations of the AI system) including the risk assessment, mitigation measures and training materials, to stakeholders such as end users and relevant authorities in alignment with regulations, while safeguarding intellectual property rights. Share information and reports to relevant stakeholders (e.g., AI Verify report). Information in the reports to be sufficiently clear and understandable to enable deployers and users as appropriate and relevant to interpret the model/system’s output and to enable users to use it appropriately. Transparency reporting to be supported and informed by robust documentation processes such as technical documentation and instructions for use.

sheet_text: Provide purpose, intended use and intended response of AI system to end users
official_text: Provide information such as the purpose, intended use and intended response of the AI system to end users

sheet_text: Align with existing data protection laws and regulations (PDPA, GDPR, etc.)
official_text: Align with existing data protection laws and regulations

sheet_text: Publish privacy policy on website: data practices, third-party disclosure, data ownership, data flow, applicable standards
official_text: Publish a privacy policy on your organization’s website to share information about the use of personal data in the AI system (e.g., data practices, and decision-making processes). The general disclosure notice could include: - Disclosure of third-party engagement - Definition of data ownership and portability - Depiction of the data flow and identify any leakages - Identification of standards the company is compliant with as assurance to customers

sheet_text: Processes in place for communication of incidents to end users
official_text: Processes in place for communication of incidents to end users

sheet_text: Processes for reporting adverse impacts, including whistleblower protection
official_text: Processes in place for reporting of adverse impacts of AI system, including protection for whistleblowers

sheet_text: Publish generic information on development/use of AI systems and AI governance approach on website
official_text: Publish generic information on the organisation's development and use of AI systems, and its approach to AI governance through channels such as organisation's website and public regulatory filings

sheet_text: Make model/system cards publicly available for AI systems warranted by public interest
official_text: Make model/system cards publicly available - in an accessible form - for specific AI systems where it is warranted by public interest or is helpful to build public trust in the organisation/ its use of AI

sheet_text: Perform analysis to determine feature contributions using technical tools (e.g., SHAP, LIME)
official_text: Perform analysis to determine feature contributions using technical tools

sheet_text: If less explainable model chosen, document rationale, risk assessment, trade-offs; apply XAI techniques (counterfactual prompts, word clouds)
official_text: If choosing a less explainable modelling approach, document the rationale, risk assessments, and trade- offs of the AI model Apply explainable AI (XAI) techniques (e.g., counterfactual prompts, word clouds) as part of ongoing continuous improvement processes to mitigate risks related to unexplainable AI systems, and verify alignment with intended purpose

sheet_text: Implement version control of source code and frameworks; track code version, parameters, hyperparameters, source data for each model version
official_text: Implement version control of source code and frameworks used to develop the model. For each version of the model, track the code version, as well as the parameters, hyperparameters, and source data used

sheet_text: Log and capture data used to train model and to produce inference results
official_text: Log and capture clearly the data used to train a model version, as well as produce inference results using the model (batch scoring or API endpoint)

sheet_text: Link inference results back to underlying model and source code
official_text: Link the inference results of the model (batch scoring or API endpoint) back to the underlying model and source code

sheet_text: Log all inputs and inference outputs; store for reasonable duration for review
official_text: Log all inputs and inference outputs of the model, and store them for a reasonable duration so that they can be reviewed

sheet_text: Version control model artefacts — associate each with code version, dependencies, parameters used in training
official_text: Version control model artefacts by associating each artefact with the version of code, dependencies, and parameters used in training

sheet_text: Calculate multiple inferences; check if output falls within accepted limits
official_text: Calculate multiple inferences; and check if the output falls within the accepted limits of the AI system owner

sheet_text: Identify combination of technical and business metrics for model assessment
official_text: Identify a combination of technical metrics and business metrics that AI models are designed to be assessed against

sheet_text: Track experiments (hyperparameters, model performance); document rationale for challenger models and final deployed model selection
official_text: Keep track of experiments (e.g., hyperparameters and model performance) used to develop challenger models, document the rationale for developing these models, and how the final deployed model was arrived at

sheet_text: Version control training input data; if not possible, avoid changing raw data and track transformation steps (preferably as DAG)
official_text: Version control the input data used for training where possible. If not possible, avoid changing the raw data at the source, and keep track of the various stages or transformation steps that are part of the data pipeline for AI model development, preferably as a directed acyclic graph (DAG)

sheet_text: Record statistical distribution of inputs/outputs; monitor parameters and metrics across retraining runs for anomalies
official_text: Record the statistical distribution of input features and output results so that divergence during retraining can be flagged. Monitor input parameters and evaluation metrics for anomalies across retraining runs

sheet_text: Log audit trail of when/how each model was deployed: code, test/validation data, model artefact version
official_text: Log audit trail of when and how each model was deployed, including the code used to serve the model, testing/validation data, and what version of the model artefact was used

sheet_text: Curate test set and apply to model to review performance
official_text: Curate the test set and apply the test set on the model to review performance

sheet_text: Identify relevant benchmarks; prepare prompts for possible harms; run benchmarking and red-teaming; test in secure environments; identify relevant stakeholders to review scores
official_text: Identify relevant and/or use-case appropriate benchmarks - prepare datasets/prompts that include questions or statements that can solicit possible harms including toxic output Document instructions given to AI red-teamers Run benchmarking and redteaming Testing to take place in secure environments and be performed at several checkpoints throughout the AI lifecycle in particular before deployment and placement on the market to identify risks and vulnerabilities, and to inform action to address the identified AI risks. The results of red-teaming conducted to evaluate the model’s/ system’s fitness for moving beyond the development stage. Identify relevant stakeholders (e.g., AI system owner, product manager, risk team) to determine if the test scores are acceptable for the use case Where applicable, share results with relevant stakeholders

sheet_text: Complete/submit Assessment of Materiality to accountable parties (AI governance committee, system owner); document justifications for decisions on materiality and application of governance controls
official_text: Complete and submit the Assessment of Materiality to the appropriate parties who are accountable for the AI system (e.g., AI governance committee, AI system owner, and reviewers) and highlight the risks of the proposed AI solution. Document the justifications for decisions on materiality and the application of relevant governance and controls to demonstrate to regulators and auditors that sufficient responsibility has been taken by humans to address potential risks. The materiality assessment could be based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, or other data. This could also be a continuous feedback process between AI system operators and stakeholders

sheet_text: Document intended use cases, capabilities, impact, limitations via model cards; conduct adversarial role-playing and chaos testing; state safeguard requirements and plans
official_text: Document the intended use cases, capabilities, impact and limitations of AI models e.g., via model cards, and approaches for model release Include relevant AI actors in the risk identification process Process to obtain feedback for risk measurement such as red- teaming and independent evaluation Conduct adversarial role-playing exercises red-teaming and chaos testing to identify possible failures State the safeguard requirements (e.g., what are the risks/failures/ unacceptable outcomes to mitigate against), safeguard plans (e.g., what are the safeguards, evaluate whether the safeguards are sufficient / working as intended to address the requirements) This documentation should be stored and retrieved together with the model artefact, as well as surfaced during a review process before the model is deployed into production

sheet_text: Conduct regular evaluation for fine-tuned models or new domains; ensure fine-tuning doesn't compromise safety/security; develop plan for post-deployment safeguard assessment
official_text: Conduct regular evaluation of risks for models that are fine-tuned, or when adapted to new domains or when risks exceeds organisational risk tolerance Ensure fine-tuning does not compromise safety and security controls Develop plan to assess the safeguards after deployment, including how frequent the assessment should occur (e.g., based on time / changes in model capability/performance) and whether the plan is sufficient

sheet_text: Assign post-deployment reviewer; include model cards to ensure alignment with intended use; share/publish performance and improvement reports
official_text: Assign a reviewer who is familiar with the downstream use case of an AI model to review the model post-deployment. This process should include model cards/documentation to ensure alignment between intended use cases at modelling and post- deployment. Where applicable, share or publish reports detailing the performance, feedback received, and improvements made

sheet_text: Use AI models that produce confidence scores; implement mechanisms to detect potential failure or data outliers
official_text: Where feasible, use AI models that can produce confidence score together with prediction. Low confidence scores may occur when the data contains values that are outside the range of the training data, or for data regions where there were insufficient training examples to make a robust estimate. Implement mechanisms to detect if model might fail or input represents an outlier in terms of training data, e.g., return some "data outlier score" with predictions

sheet_text: Continuous monitoring of third-party systems and fallback plan; establish contracts with clear liability; contingency processes for failures or overreliance on third-party systems
official_text: Continuous monitoring of third party systems and fallback plan that monitors the effectiveness of risk controls and mitigation plans Establish proper contracts with third parties, with clear assignment of liability and responsibilities Contingency processes to handle failures or incidents (e.g., arising from third-party data or AI systems that are high risk or data redundancy such as model weights and other system artifacts) or overreliance on third party data and systems

sheet_text: Implement deployment strategies such as blue-green and canary deployments
official_text: Implement deployment strategies such as blue- green and canary deployments

sheet_text: Maintain backup model server in blue-green deployment mode
official_text: Maintain backup model server in blue-green deployment mode

sheet_text: Use AI models that produce confidence scores; design systems to handle failure/low confidence; fall back to backup servers or sensible defaults
official_text: Where feasible, use AI models that can produce a confidence score together with the prediction. Design the systems that are using the results of the AI model to handle cases where the model fails or has low confidence, falling back to backup model servers or sensible default behaviour

sheet_text: Close feedback loop by retraining models with ground truth obtained in production
official_text: Close the feedback loop by retraining models with ground truth obtained once models are in production

sheet_text: Document residual risk assessment and reasons for tolerance level; implement risk tracking approaches for difficult-to-measure risks
official_text: Document the assessment of the residual risk and provide reasons for the tolerance level Risk tracking approaches are considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available. For risks difficult to assess or where metrics are not available, put in place risk tracking approaches such as developing a risk reporting matrix, communicating potential risk to affected stakeholders, monitoring risk mitigation plans and reviewing status updates regularly

sheet_text: Assess harms (bias, IP infringement, CSAM, CBRN info, offensive cyber); implement guardrails, content filters, human moderation; monitor output for socio-cultural alignment
official_text: Assess existence or level of harms (e.g., bias, intellectual property infringement). Identify content that may violate laws and regulations (e.g., child sexual abuse material (CSAM), non-consensus intimate image (NCII)), inappropriate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) information), offensive cyber capabilities) Implement measures to prevent AI model from generating such content (e.g., guardrails, content filters, human moderation system) and mitigating steps should it happens (e.g., integrate feedback into AI system updates). Document the mechanisms to prevent AI model from generating content that violates laws and regulations. Monitor and review output regularly for validity, safety, and aligned with socio-cultural norms, trigger alerts for intervention (e.g., use of sentiment analysis to gauge user sentiment)

sheet_text: Understand AI limits; identify provenance harms (deepfakes); identify methods to trace digital content origin (e.g., C2PA); integrate real-time monitoring; maintain change records
official_text: For Use. Understand the AI system's limits, how its output may be utilised and how the AI system interacts with external networks. Identify potential content provenance harms such as deepfakes. Conduct feedback on expectations, concerns, generated content and labels on content. Use feedback to guide design of provenance data-tracking techniques. Identify methods to trace and analyse the origin and modifications of digital content (e.g., c2pa). Provenance data to include an identifier of the service or model that created the content. Integrate tools to enable real- time monitoring of each instance when content is generated, modified or shared, identify data anomalies and verify authenticity of digital content (e.g., digital signatures). Maintain records of changes to content including content by third parties. Implement content provenance management with third parties

sheet_text: Implement evaluation metrics by demographic groups; manage statistical bias in content provenance; measure effectiveness of watermarking; apply TEVV practices
official_text: For evaluation. Implement evaluation metrics by demographic groups to identify discrepancies in how content provenance mechanisms work across diverse populations. Manage statistical bias related to content provenance through techniques such as re-sampling or adversarial training. Measure effectiveness and reliability of content provenance methodologies such as watermark. Apply TEVV practices for content provenance (e.g., probing a system's synthetic data generation capabilities for potential misuse). Assess how well solutions address risks or harms

sheet_text: For experimental systems, document TEVV considerations; assess accuracy, quality, reliability by comparing to ground truth; conduct adversarial testing
official_text: For systems that are in experimental stage, put in place a process to document the TEVV considerations. For example, creation of measurement error models for pre-deployment metrics to demonstrate construct validity for each metric. Assess the accuracy, quality, reliability and authenticity of output by comparing to ground truth, and conducting adversarial testing to identify vulnerabilities, potential manipulation or misuse of the system

sheet_text: Document fact-checking techniques; use testing techniques to identify AI- vs human-generated content
official_text: Document fact-checking techniques to verify accuracy of information and retention policy to keep history for TEVV. Use testing techniques to identify AI-generated content and human- generated content

sheet_text: Provide training and guidance on AI security risks to all personnel including developers, system owners, senior leaders
official_text: Provide adequate training and guidance on the security risks of AI to all personnel, including developers, system owners and senior leaders

sheet_text: Apply holistic process to model threats/risks (CIA triad, NIST AI RMF, OWASP SSDLC); identify metrics reflecting effectiveness of security measures
official_text: Apply a holistic process to model threats and risks to an AI system, in accordance with relevant industry standards/best practices. This includes identifying metrics that reflect the effectiveness of security measures

sheet_text: Assess and monitor supply chain security risks; ensure suppliers adhere to security standards; evaluate components via code checking or vulnerability databases
official_text: Assess and monitor potential security risks of the AI system’s supply chain across its life cycle Ensure that suppliers adhere to policy and security standards, or that risks are otherwise appropriately managed. Consider evaluating supply chain components (e.g. through code checking, or against vulnerability databases)

sheet_text: When developing/selecting AI model, consider security factors: complexity, explainability, interpretability, sensitivity of training data
official_text: When developing or selecting an appropriate AI model for your system, consider factors which may affect its security (such as complexity, explainability, interpretability, and sensitivity of training data)

sheet_text: Understand value of AI assets (models, data, prompts, logs); track, authenticate, version control and secure all assets
official_text: Understand the value of AI-related assets, including models, data, prompts, logs and assessments. Have processes to track, authenticate, version control, and secure assets

sheet_text: Apply standard infrastructure security: access controls, logging/monitoring, segregation of environments, secure-by-default configurations
official_text: Apply standard infrastructure security principles, such as implementing appropriate access controls and logging/monitoring, segregation of environments, and secure-by-default configurations

sheet_text: Apply infrastructure security: access controls, logging/monitoring, segregation, secure-by-default, firewalls; ensure contingency plans for disruption/failure
official_text: Apply standard infrastructure security principles, such as access controls and logging/monitoring, segregation of environments, secure- by-default configurations, and firewalls

sheet_text: Put in place incident response, escalation and remediation plans; apply logging/auditing guidance; reassess plans as system changes; report to relevant stakeholders
official_text: Put in place appropriate incident response, escalation and remediation plans

sheet_text: Subject AI systems to appropriate security checks before release; verify model/data signatures and hashes; benchmark and test before release
official_text: Release models, applications or systems only after subjecting them to appropriate and effective security checks and evaluation

sheet_text: Monitor and log inputs (queries, prompts, requests) for attacks and suspicious activity; monitor/limit rate of queries
official_text: Monitor and log inputs to the AI system, such as queries, prompts and requests. Proper logging allows for compliance, audit, investigation and remediation

sheet_text: Monitor model outputs and performance post-deployment; ensure adequate human oversight to verify output; monitor for anomalous behaviour
official_text: Monitoring models after deployment to make sure they are performing as intended, and alert system owners to potential issues (whether caused by adversarial attacks or otherwise)

sheet_text: Treat major updates as new versions; integrate software and model updates together; treat new training input data as new data
official_text: Ensure risks associated to model updates have been considered and appropriately managed

sheet_text: Put in place feedback process for users to share findings of concern; communicate findings to appropriate stakeholders and authorities
official_text: Put in place a feedback process for users to share any findings of concern, which might uncover potential vulnerabilities to the system

sheet_text: Implement secure disposal/destruction of data and models per relevant standards and regulations (e.g., crypto shredding, degaussing)
official_text: Implement proper and secure disposal/destruction of data and models in accordance with relevant industry standards or regulations

sheet_text: Traditional: calculate accuracy metrics; add noise and compare. Generative: benchmarking with relevant datasets; add perturbations (synonym, typo, punctuation) and test against same metric
official_text: Traditional AI - Calculate accuracy metrics at testing time. Add noise to dataset and compare the 2 accuracy metrics (between the dataset with and dataset without noise). The accuracy metric is calculated based on the matching ground truth labels against the predictions. Generative AI - Benchmarking (to compare AI model's performance against time / another model), with datasets that are relevant to the use cas e. For example, adding noise / perturbate (invariance testing such as synonym, typo, punctuation or adversarial perturbation) to the original prompts in the benchmark and tested against the same metric

sheet_text: Ensure data is up-to-date, complete, representative; log training run metadata; monitor production vs training data for data/concept drift
official_text: - Implement measures to ensure data is up-to-date, complete, and representative of the environment the system will be deployed in - Log training run metadata to do comparison in production, e.g., parameters, and version model to monitor model staleness - Monitor production versus training data characteristics at production stage e.g., statistical distribution, data types, and validation constraints, to detect data and concept drift

sheet_text: Document intended use cases, risks, and limitations (e.g., model cards)
official_text: Document intended use cases, risks, limitations (e.g., in model cards)

sheet_text: Document intended use cases, risks, limitations in model cards
official_text: Document intended use cases, risks, limitations (e.g., in model cards)

sheet_text: Implement review process highlighting changes in code (training, serving), input data, and output data
official_text: Implement a review process that highlights changes in code (e.g., training, serving), input data (e.g., raw data, features), and output data (e.g., inference results, performance metrics)

sheet_text: Implement methods to mitigate known adversarial attacks at training time
official_text: Implement methods to mitigate known adversarial attacks at training time, including decisions whether to adopt / not adopt the methods. Note: It may not be possible for all models (e.g., if the model is deterministic or with a model with high level of interactivity with users)

sheet_text: Monitor requests to live AI system (frequency, feature distribution) to detect suspicious use
official_text: Monitor requests made to live AI system, e.g., frequency and feature distribution of queries, in order to detect whether it is being used suspiciously

sheet_text: Take action on users with suspicious activity: flag for review, rate-limit, block, suspend accounts
official_text: Take action on users who exhibit suspicious activity, e.g., flag for review, rate-limit or block further requests, suspend user accounts

sheet_text: Establish policy for continuous monitoring and periodic validation: model performance (feature drift, inference drift, accuracy), application performance (latency, error rates), regular safety reviews (guardrails)
official_text: Establish policy to evaluate, continuous monitor and conduct periodic validation of the quality of the model's output, capabilities and robustness of safety measures before and after models have gone live. This includes: - Model performance, e.g., monitor feature drift, inference drift, accuracy against ground truth - Application performance, e.g., latency, throughput, error rates, near- misses, and negative impacts - Continuously assess the quality of the output(s) of the AI system and ensure that the operating conditions of a live AI system match the thesis under which it was originally developed - Evaluate AI system performance in real-world scenarios to observe its behaviour in practical environments and reveal issues that might not surface in controlled and optimized testing environments - Regular review of safety of the AI system (e.g., implement and assess guardrails)

sheet_text: Establish policy on extent of human domain knowledge used (RLHF, fine-tuning, RAG); review/verify sources and citations; track anthropomorphising instances
official_text: Establish policy that: - States extent of human domain knowledge used to improve the AI system (e.g., RLHF, fine tuning, retrieval-augmented generation) - Review and verify sources and citations in generated output - Track instances of anthropomorphising in AI system (where applicable)

sheet_text: AI system owner selects fairness metrics for sensitive feature; measure disparity of error rates across groups
official_text: AI system owner decides on the fairness metrics for the sensitive feature. To measures the disparity of error rates across groups, based on the selected fairness metrics

sheet_text: Identify relevant benchmarks; prepare prompts for possible harms against individuals/groups; run benchmarking and red-teaming; identify stakeholders to review scores
official_text: Identify relevant and/or use-case appropriate benchmarks - prepare datasets/prompts that include questions or statements that can solicit possible harms including toxic output against individuals or groups Document instructions given to AI red-teamers Run benchmarking and redteaming Identify relevant stakeholders (e.g., AI system owner, product manager, risk team) to determine if the test scores are acceptable for the use case Where applicable, share results with relevant stakeholders

sheet_text: Apply counterfactual fairness assessment
official_text: Apply counterfactual fairness assessment

sheet_text: Monitor changes in fairness metric values throughout AI lifecycle
official_text: Monitor the changes in fairness metric values in the lifecycle of the AI system.

sheet_text: Consider using Fairness Decision Tree (AI Verify, Aequitas); select metrics: Equal Parity, Disparate Impact, FNR/FPR Parity, etc.
official_text: Consider using Fairness Decision Tree (e.g., AI Verify, Aequitas) to select the appropriate metric(s) for your application

sheet_text: Identify sensitive features and their privileged/unprivileged groups; refer to local guidelines (Singapore Tripartite Guidelines, UK Equality Act)
official_text: Identify the sensitive features and their privileged and unprivileged groups where feasible

sheet_text: Consult impacted communities on correct definition of fairness; include values and considerations of those impacted (elderly, persons with disabilities)
official_text: Where feasible, consult the impacted communities on the correct definition of fairness (e.g., representatives of elderly persons or persons with disabilities), values and considerations of those impacted (e.g., individual's preference)

sheet_text: Perform exploratory data analysis; test representation of each group; resample or collect more data if group is underrepresented, data is homogenous, or GAI-produced
official_text: Perform exploratory data analysis. Test the representation of each group in the data. To mitigate concerns of model collapse, resample data or collect more data if: - a particular group is severely underrepresented or - training data is overly homogenous or - GAI-produced

sheet_text: Monitor threshold violations of fairness metrics post-deployment; obtain feedback from those impacted; offer redress and remediation options
official_text: Monitor threshold violations of fairness metrics post- deployment and for actual harms

sheet_text: Monitor metrics for latest data of currently deployed model on an ongoing basis
official_text: Monitor metrics for the latest set of data for the model currently being deployed on an ongoing basis.

sheet_text: Handle imbalanced training sets: oversample minority, undersample majority, or generate synthetic samples (SMOTE)
official_text: Where possible, handle imbalanced training sets with minorities. Examples: - Oversample minority class - Undersample majority class - Generate synthetic samples (SMOTE)

sheet_text: Verify quality: accuracy, completeness, veracity, recency, relevance, integrity, usability; distribution analysis; seek feedback from stakeholders
official_text: Verify the quality of data used in the AI system, including intellectual property and privacy risks as well as unsafe content (e.g., CBRN). This may include the following: - accuracy in terms of how well the values in the dataset match the true characteristics of the entity described by the dataset - completeness in terms of attributes and items e.g., checking for missing values, duplicate records - veracity in terms of how credible the data is, including whether the data originated from a reliable source - How recently the dataset was compiled or updated - Relevance for the intended purpose - Integrity in terms of how well extraction and transformation have been performed if multiple datasets are joined; - Usability in terms of how the data are tracked and stored in a consistent, human-readable format - Providing distribution analysis e.g., feature distributions of input data - Seek feedback from relevant stakeholders

sheet_text: Maintain data provenance record: data collection process, evaluation of data/content flow, labelling process, bias assessment, data transformation tracking, PII anonymisation
official_text: Maintain a data provenance record to ascertain the quality of the data based on its origin and subsequent transformation. This could include the following: - Take steps to understand the meaning of and how data was collected, including known assumptions and practices - Evaluate data and content flow within AI systems - Document data usage and related concerns - Ensure any data labelling is done by a representative group of labellers and instructions are provided - Document the procedure for assessing labels for bias - Trace potential sources of errors - Update to data and monitoring other changes that may impact the verifiability of content origins - Attribute data to their sources - Anonymise data, leverage privacy output filters, remove personally identifiable information (PII)

sheet_text: Ensure data protection, consent, collection, use, retention, withdrawal carried out per regulations (PDPA, European Data Governance Act, APEC CBPR); remove CBRN info and IP from training data
official_text: Ensure that data protection, consent, collection, use, withdrawal, retention and assessment has been carried out in accordance with the relevant regulatory requirements and/or industry standards. Disclose policies and practices where appropriate. Mitigation steps have been taken. For example: - review training data for CBRN information, and intellectual property, and where appropriate, remove it. - Implement measures to prevent, flag, or take other action in response to outputs that reproduce particular training data (e.g., plagiarized, trademarked, patented, licensed content or trade secret material)

sheet_text: Detect personally identifiable information or sensitive data in generated output; implement anonymisation, synthetic data, privacy enhancing technologies
official_text: Detect presence of personally identifiable information or sensitive data in generated output Implement techniques such as anonymisation, synthetic data generation and privacy enhancing technologies to minimise risks associated with linking AI-generated content back to humans

sheet_text: Ensure relevant team members know roles and responsibilities for data governance; may include a data policy team to manage data lineage tracking
official_text: Ensure that relevant team members are knowledgeable about their roles and responsibilities for data governance. Relevant team members include any employee that is involved in managing and using the data for the AI system. For example, having a data policy team to manage the tracking of data lineage with proper controls

sheet_text: Categorise third-party content types (copyright, IP); implement practices for third-party data storage/collection; monitor outputs for privacy/disclosure risks; respond to IP infringement claims
official_text: Categorise different types of content associated with third party rights (e.g., copyright, intellectual property) to be informed on the use of external data Implement practices on how third party intellectual property and training data will be used, stored and collected Conduct monitoring of output for privacy risk and data disclosure Implement process to respond to potential intellectual property infringement claims or other rights Educate relevant stakeholders such as third parties on best practices for managing risks Obtain feedback and recommendations from organizational boards or committees when using third-party pre-trained models

sheet_text: Identify acceptable/unacceptable/illegal AI uses; engage end users on expectations; implement recourse mechanisms; compile violations; review AI policy regularly
official_text: Identify acceptable, unacceptable and illegal uses of AI model and output, including criteria for the AI model not respond to (e.g., queries to chatbots) Process to engage end users on their expectations and needs (e.g. providing general usage agreements that scope its use) Incorporate relevant stakeholders such as end users’ expectations/ needs in the responsible development and use of the AI system Implement mechanisms for recourse Compile violations, take-down requests, intellectual property infringement AI policy reviewed regularly to ensure its continued suitability, adequacy and effectiveness, proportional to the identified risks, including making adjustments to organisational roles and components

sheet_text: Document use, norms and expectations for deployment; include relevant stakeholders (users, domain experts, socio-cultural experts) and their interactions with the AI system
official_text: Refer to 4.2 and 4.3. In addition, document the use, norms and expectations in which the AI system will be deployed. Considerations to include relevant stakeholders (e.g., users, domain and socio-cultural experts), and how they interact with the AI system

sheet_text: Select AI suppliers aligned with organisation's approach; establish processes to take remedial action when suppliers do not perform as intended
official_text: Select AI system suppliers which align with organisation’s approach. When AI system suppliers do not perform as intended, there are processes to take remedial actions.

sheet_text: Put in place manual for AI model deactivation (data security, retention, leakage, user dependency); communications plan for deactivation/disengagement
official_text: Put in place a: - manual on how to deactivate AI model while considering factors such as data security, retention and leakage, as well as users' dependency on the AI model - communications plan to inform AI stakeholders as part of deactivation or disengagement process

sheet_text: Adapt existing structures, communication lines, procedures, rules (e.g., three lines of defence model) or implement new ones
official_text: Adapt existing structures, communication lines, procedures, and rules (e.g., three lines of defence risk management model) or implement new ones

sheet_text: Establish AI governance committee with representatives from data science, technology, risk, legal, product, UX/ethics; integrate into existing risk/compliance structures if committee not practical
official_text: For organisations who are using AI across departments, establish teams or AI governance committee that comprises representatives from data science, technology, risk, and product to facilitate cross-departmental oversight for the lifecycle governance of AI systems If it's not practical to have cross-department oversight, integrate accountability of the use of AI into existing risk or compliance structures For systems with national security risks, involve relevant stakeholders

sheet_text: Develop and implement policies, procedures, training to ensure staff familiarity with duties and risk management practices
official_text: Develop and implement policies, procedures, and training to ensure that staff are familiar with their duties and the organisation’s risk management practices

sheet_text: Enable incident management process: report on actions affecting AI outcomes; review and update processes at appropriate junctures; verify incident response teams have appropriate skills
official_text: Enable an incident management process: - processes and mechanisms to report on actions or decisions that affect the AI system's outcome in compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, and a corresponding process for the accountable party to respond to the consequences of such an outcome - the above processes and mechanisms to be reviewed and updated at appropriate junctures - for incident monitoring and reporting, including verifying information and having a minimum set of criteria for reporting such as stakeholders impacted - to verify teams that conduct incident response demonstrate appropriate skills and training as well as have a diverse composition and responsibilities based on the particular incident type - to measure the rate at which recommendations from security checks and incidents are implemented, and assess how quickly the AI system can adapt and improve - that safeguards intellectual property rights

sheet_text: Implement fine-grained access control: code/data for training, code/data for deployment, execution environments, permissions for actions (training job, review, deploy), admin functions
official_text: Implement fine-grained access control that aligns with various roles for users: - Access to code and data for training AI models - Access to code and data for deploying AI models - Access to different execution environments - Permission to perform various actions (e.g., launch training job, review model, deploy model server) - Permission to define access control rules and perform other administrative functions

sheet_text: Communicate responsibilities to all parties; implement SLAs and contracts with third parties (content provenance, usage rights, security requirements); conduct third-party vendor risk assessment
official_text: Responsibilities and obligations are clearly communicated to all parties related to the AI system Implement service level agreements and contracts with third parties that specify requirements, expectation and evaluation e.g. content provenance, usage rights, security requirements Implement a risk assessment framework to evaluate and monitor third parties' performance (e.g., content provenance standards) Conduct assessment on third parties or vendors, including AI risks and benefits arising from use of third party models or resources such as: - application of organisational risk tolerance - value chain risks - transparency artifacts (e.g., model and system cards) for third party models

sheet_text: Process/technology to handle: version control of code and model, version data or maintain immutable data, audit trail of deployment history, log inputs/outputs
official_text: Process or technology should handle: - Version control of code and model - Version data or maintain immutable data - Audit trail of deployment history, log inputs/outputs, associate server predictions with the originating model

sheet_text: Evaluate necessity of third-party models; demonstrate effort to understand how they were built: training data, effectiveness assessment, failure circumstances
official_text: Evaluate the necessity of third-party models e.g., they are trained on data otherwise not accessible to your organisation ,or you do not have the requisite capability to build AI systems in-house

sheet_text: Understand how third-party models were built: training data, effectiveness assessment, explainability, failure conditions
official_text: Demonstrate effort to understand how the third-party models were built, including 1) what data was used to train the models, 2) how the models are assessed for effectiveness and explainability 3) under what circumstances does the AI system perform poorly

sheet_text: Engage external AI actors for feedback pre/post-deployment; define beneficial use cases for feedback; ensure representative and diverse outreach; develop metrics to evaluate feedback; identify emerging best practices
official_text: In addition to 7.7.1, - Put in place a process to engage external AI actors for feedback pre- deployment and post-deployment - Define use case where feedback exercise would be beneficial - Ensure regular outreach and feedback exercises are representative and diverse. The exercises can include studies, prototyping and testing activities (e.g. test of AI capabilities, human proficiency tests), how users perceive the output from the AI model, to identify or review unanticipated impacts, or to detect subtle shifts in quality or alignment of AI model output with community and societal values. - Allocate time and resources for outreach, feedback and recourse processes, including prioritising feedback based on risk assessment - Verify adequacy of user instructions through using testing - Develop metrics to evaluate the feedback - Identify emerging best practices and technologies in measuring and managing identified risks Where applicable, verify those conducting feedback are not directly involved in system development task for the AI model

sheet_text: Conduct impact assessment on use of AI vs non-AI alternative systems and resources required to manage risk
official_text: Conduct impact assessment on the use of AI verses non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods, and the resources required to manage the risk of using AI

sheet_text: Put in place guided flow for documenting AI system inventory, necessary resources, risk priorities, and exemptions (e.g., GAI systems embedded in software)
official_text: Put in place guided flow for documenting (i) the inventory of AI systems and necessary resources (e.g., data, tooling, system & computing and human resources), (ii) risk priorities and (iii) inventory exemptions (e.g. GAI systems embedded into application software). This include inventory of all third party entities. Data include data provenance information such as watermark, signatures, versioning System include bug tracking or external information sharing resource

sheet_text: Reviewers should be distinct from those training and deploying models
official_text: Reviewers should be distinct from those who are training and deploying models. However, it is acceptable to have the same individuals training and deploying models

sheet_text: Guided flow for documenting important info (model cards, forms, SDK); document processes providing objective decision-making criteria (e.g., fairness metrics selection)
official_text: Put in place guided flow for documenting (i) important info via model cards, forms, SDK library; and (ii) important processes that provide objective criteria for decision-making (e.g., fairness metrics selection)

sheet_text: Implement data management system to gather and organise relevant information based on different user role needs
official_text: Implement a data management system to gather and organise relevant information based needs of different user roles reviewing models, and monitoring live systems) EVIDENCE Internal documentation (e.g., procedure manual, log, register, or database) Documentary evidence of data management system to gather and based on the needs of different user roles

sheet_text: Define role of human in oversight and control (human-in-the-loop, human-out-the-loop, human-over-the-loop); establish escalation pathways for high-risk AI systems
official_text: Define the role of the human in its oversight and control of the AI system (e.g., human-in-the-loop, human-out-the-loop, human-over- the-loop)

sheet_text: Design system to flag cases where AI is significantly unsure; monitor instances where human operators override AI decisions
official_text: When the AI model is making a decision for which it is significantly unsure of the answer/prediction, consider designing the system to be able to flag these cases and triage them for a human to review Monitor and evaluate the instances where human operators or other systems override the GAI's decisions

sheet_text: Implement mechanisms to detect if model input represents outlier in terms of training data (e.g., data outlier score)
official_text: Implement mechanisms to detect if model input represents an outlier in terms of training data (e.g., return some "data outlier score" with predictions)

sheet_text: Implement systematic review process to present performance, explainability, and fairness metrics understandable to data science, product, legal/risk, ethics teams
official_text: Implement a systematic review process to present performance, explainability, and fairness metrics in a way that is understandable by data science, product, legal and risk, experience research, and ethics teams

sheet_text: After production, put in place mechanisms for ongoing model performance review: time-based (every 2 years) or event-based (new AI product, new data, changed context, substantial modification)
official_text: After models are put into production, put in place mechanisms to review the performance of the models on an ongoing basis, either continuously or at regular intervals. Criteria could be time-based (e.g., every 2 years) or event-based (before the launch of a new AI product, after the introduction of new data, operating context has changed due to external circumstances), or when the AI system has undergone substantial modification

sheet_text: Declaration of transparency on how and where in the decision-making process AI complements or replaces human
official_text: Declaration of transparency on how and where in the decision- making process the AI system is used to complement or replace the human

sheet_text: Conduct environmental impact assessment; address energy, water, carbon capture, green-washing concerns; monitor energy and waste consumption
official_text: Put in place a process to determine that the development and deployment of the AI system is for the benefit of the environment, where applicable. For example: - conduct impact assessment on the natural environment, and take measures to minimise negative impact (e.g., pollution) - address environmental concerns (e.g., energy and water consumption, carbon capture and green washing concerns) - monitor energy and waste consumptions The above could be carried out through interviews with relevant stakeholders and impact studies

sheet_text: Conduct societal impact assessment: life, health, work, skills; take measures to minimise negative impact on human capabilities, jobs, skills, creative economies, discriminatory norms
official_text: Put in place a process to determine that the development and deployment of the AI system is for the benefit of people and society, where applicable. For example, conduct impact assessment on societal implications such as life, health, work and skills and take measures to minimise negative impact The above could be carried out through interviews with relevant stakeholders and impact studies
